neighbours.label: A verb of informing or directing someone, where a pronoun object comes next ('told them', 'let them know', 'tell it to'); the same requests with no one addressed stay low.
fire: We rang the airline right away and told them to cancel the booking.
Please email the front desk to let them know when you arrive.
The installer leaves your files alone unless you tell it to.
My neighbours were away, so I phoned and told them about the leak.
If you can't make it, call the office and let them know.
She went to the landlord and told him the heating had failed.
Walk up to the guard and tell him you have an appointment.
The kids were noisy until I finally told them to stop.
quiet: We rang the airline right away and paid the booking fee.
Please email the front desk with your arrival time.
The installer leaves your files alone during the update.
My neighbours were away, so I fixed the leak myself.
If you can't make it, the office will close at five.
She went to the landlord's house and paid the rent in cash.
Walk up to the gate and sign in for your appointment.
The kids were noisy until the film finally started.
